name: Harness Skills
description: Every message: the agent picks a lane (small, medium or full) before its first edit.

action.text: Before your first edit, read the code the request touches and list the choices that belong to the user: behaviour, interface, scope, data, cost or delivery that neither the request nor the code settles. A small request can hold one (does a delete need a confirmation or an undo?). When one is open, load the us-grill-me skill, ask, and end your turn with no edit and no status table: a question is not your final answer. Never ask what the request or the code already answers, and do not ask when the request is precise. Status line: "Questions: asked 2" or "Questions: none open". Then rate the complexity of the request and state it in one line: "Complexity: small | medium | full — reason". small (a typo, a one-liner, an obvious bug, a copy tweak): do it and verify, with no workflow stages. medium (a bounded fix or tweak across a few files, no new feature): implement it yourself, then run the enabled review and security review stages, with no scout and no planner or approval. full (a new view, new functionality, a refactor, a data, storage or architecture change, or unclear scope): load the us-run-workflow skill (Harness Skills) and run its full lane: scout research, planner with approval, implementation by workers, reviews, release assessment and memory. Before you open any PR, whatever the tier, run the us-assess-release skill on the final commit and put its Review guide in the PR body, unless the release-assessment setting is off.
